content: Ranunculus acris, commonly referred to as Meadow Buttercup, Tall Buttercup, or Tall Field Buttercup, is one of the most widespread buttercup species found across Europe and temperate regions of Eurasia. This plant is characterized by its somewhat hairy appearance and ascending, flowing stems that bear glossy yellow flowers approximately 25 millimeters in diameter. Each flower consists of five overlapping petals situated above five green sepals, which gradually turn yellow as the flower matures. The plant also features numerous stamens positioned below the ovary. Ranunculus acris typically blooms from May to July. Like other members of the Ranunculus genus, its seeds are produced as achenes. When the plant is handled, a naturally occurring compound called ranunculin is broken down into protoanemonin. Protoanemonin is known to cause contact dermatitis in humans, necessitating caution when handling the plant excessively. However, the toxins in the plant are degraded through drying, making hay containing dried buttercups safe for use.
